The majority of people that want to get their hands on a cryptocurrency such as Bitcoin (BTC) will simply purchase coins from friends or an online exchange. All you have to do to get started with cryptocurrency trading is look up an online trading platform on Btxchange.io , create an account and you’re good to go! Another, less common method to obtain Bitcoin is though mining it.
This method is getting trickier as cryptocurrencies become more popular, with more expensive mining hardware needed as well as a lot of power, often not even profitable for individuals.
Therefore, many people will choose to join a mining pool. If you are deciding whether joining a mining pool is right for you, there are many pros and cons to consider. Of course, going solo means that you will get the reward all to yourself, but the odds of getting the reward are dramatically decreased.
If you are in a pool, there is much more of a chance that you will solve a mining block, but then you will have to share the reward with the others.
Therefore, if you are trying to earn money using a mining pool, although the payments may be modest, you can at least ensure that there will be a steady stream of income.
In term of Bitcoin mining, the difficulty level is so high that it is basically impossible for individuals to make any profit at all through the mining process if they are going solo. If you are just beginning in the industry, then a mining pool is probably the best way to go.
Bitcoin is, of course, not the only currency out there waiting to be mined. There are hundreds of mining pools out there for a range of different cryptocurrencies, and you can find lists of different pools for each type of digital coin.
If you are completely new to mining and don’t have particularly powerful hardware, then it might be better to take a look at various altcoins over Bitcoin.
